name: Social Studies
topics: Different houses · Jobs and communities · City and countryside · Migration and refugees · Homes

licoes.texto: Maps have tools that help us read them:
pontos: Title: tells what the map shows.
Map key (legend): tells what the symbols mean.
Compass rose: shows the directions: North, South, East, West.
Scale: helps measure real distances.
A globe is a round model of the Earth. The Equator divides it into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres.
licoes.fala: Never Eat Soggy Waffles: North, East, South, West around the compass!

licoes.texto: The Earth has 7 continents and 5 oceans.
pontos: Continents: Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Australia (Oceania), Europe, North America, South America.
Oceans: Pacific (the largest), Atlantic, Indian, Arctic, Southern.
Brazil is in South America, and its coast is on the Atlantic Ocean.
Antarctica is the coldest continent.
licoes.fala: From Brazil, I'd have to cross the whole Atlantic Ocean to get to Africa!

licoes.texto: A community is a place where people live, work and play together.
pontos: Urban: a city, with tall buildings, many people and traffic.
Suburban: near a city, with houses and yards.
Rural: the countryside, with farms and fields.
Community helpers: firefighters, doctors, teachers, police officers.
licoes.fala: Grandpa lives on a farm, a rural community. I live in the city, an urban community!

licoes.texto: We learn about the past through our families.
pontos: A family tree shows the members and generations of a family.
Your grandparents' parents are your great-grandparents.
A timeline shows events in the order they happened.
Primary sources come from the time of the event: old letters, photos, diaries.
licoes.fala: Our family tree for the Mostra Cultural has four generations!

licoes.texto: Some things we need to live. Others we just want.
pontos: Needs: food, clean water, shelter (a home), clothing.
Wants: toys, video games, candy, a skateboard.
Saving money helps us buy things later.
licoes.fala: I want a new skateboard, but first I need lunch!

pontos: Goods are things you can touch: bread, shoes, books.
Services are jobs people do for others: a haircut, a doctor visit, a bus ride.
Producers make goods or give services. Consumers buy and use them.
licoes.fala: The bread from the bakery is a good. The haircut at the salon is a service!

pontos: Rules and laws keep us safe and help us live together.
Rights: things everyone deserves, like going to school.
Responsibilities: things we should do, like doing homework and respecting others.
licoes.fala: Picking up trash in the schoolyard is a responsibility we all share!

pontos: The capital is Brasília.
Brazil has 5 regions and 26 states plus the Federal District.
Independence Day: September 7th (1822).
October 12th: Our Lady of Aparecida holiday and Children's Day.
licoes.fala: September 7th was a holiday in our school calendar. Now I know why!

questions.q: Which home is made of snow and ice?
questions.fb: O igloo é construído com blocos de neve em regiões árticas. A neve é um bom isolante — segura o calor dentro.

questions.q: Why are stilt houses built on tall wooden poles?
opts: To protect the house from floods and water
To make the house look taller
To keep the house warm in the snow
questions.fb: As palafitas ficam erguidas sobre estacas para a água das cheias passar por baixo — comuns em rios e áreas alagadas.

questions.q: An adobe house is made of:
opts: Mud, water and straw dried in the sun
questions.fb: O adobe é um tijolo de barro, água e palha, seco ao sol. Mantém a casa fresca em regiões quentes e secas.

questions.q: Why are houses different around the world?
opts: Because of the climate, the available materials and the local culture
Because some countries have no builders
Because of the day they were built
questions.fb: O clima, os materiais que existem no lugar e a cultura decidem o formato da casa. Por isso o igloo e a palafita são tão diferentes.

questions.q: Which home can be moved from one place to another?
questions.fb: A yurt é a tenda redonda usada por povos nômades da Mongólia: pode ser desmontada e levada junto com o rebanho.

questions.q: Who designs a house before it is built?
questions.fb: O arquiteto desenha a planta. Depois o builder constrói, o electrician faz a parte elétrica e o plumber cuida da água.

questions.q: Who works with water pipes in a house?
questions.fb: O plumber (encanador) instala e conserta os canos. O electrician cuida da fiação e o carpenter trabalha com madeira.

questions.q: What does urban mean?
questions.fb: Urban = da cidade (muitos prédios, trânsito, lojas). Rural = do campo (fazendas, mais natureza, menos gente).

questions.q: Which is typical of a rural area?
questions.fb: A área rural tem fazendas, plantações e poucos moradores. A urbana tem prédios, comércio e muita gente.

questions.q: What is migration?
opts: When people move from one place to another to live
When people travel on holiday and come back
When people build a new house in the same street
questions.fb: Migração é mudar de lugar para viver. Pode ser dentro do próprio país ou para outro país.

questions.q: Who is a refugee?
opts: Someone who had to leave their home because of war, danger or disaster
Someone who lives in the countryside
questions.fb: O refugiado não escolheu sair: foi forçado por guerra, perseguição ou desastre. Por isso precisa de proteção e acolhimento.

questions.q: Why do people migrate to another place?
opts: To look for work, safety, study or a better life
Because houses are all the same everywhere
questions.fb: As razões mais comuns são trabalho, segurança, estudo e saúde — a busca por uma vida melhor.

questions.q: What makes a house become a home?
opts: The people who live there and the feeling of safety and belonging
questions.fb: “House” é a construção; “home” é o lar. O que transforma uma na outra são as pessoas, as memórias e a sensação de segurança.

questions.q: What is a bungalow?
opts: A house with only one floor
questions.fb: Bungalow é a casa térrea, de um andar só.

questions.q: What is a block of flats (apartment building)?
opts: A tall building where many families live in separate homes
A house for one family only
questions.fb: Em inglês britânico é block of flats; em americano, apartment building.

questions.q: Where would you find a houseboat?
questions.fb: A houseboat é uma casa-barco, ancorada em rios e canais.

questions.q: A tipi is a traditional home of which people?
questions.fb: O tipi é a tenda cônica dos povos nativos americanos — portátil, feita de varas e peles.

questions.q: Which people traditionally build igloos?
questions.fb: Os Inuit, povos do Ártico, constroem igloos com blocos de neve.

questions.q: Who works with wood, making doors, floors and furniture?
questions.fb: O carpenter (marceneiro) trabalha com madeira.

questions.q: Who lays the bricks to build the walls?
questions.fb: O bricklayer assenta os tijolos. O builder é o termo geral para quem constrói.

questions.q: Which workers help a community stay safe and healthy?
opts: Doctors, nurses, firefighters and police officers
questions.fb: Uma comunidade precisa de muitos trabalhos diferentes: saúde, segurança, educação e construção.

questions.q: What is a community?
opts: A group of people who live in the same place and help each other
questions.fb: Comunidade é o grupo de pessoas que vive num mesmo lugar e depende umas das outras.

questions.q: Which of these is usually found in a city?
opts: Shops, offices, buses and tall buildings
questions.fb: A cidade (urban area) tem comércio, escritórios, transporte e muitos prédios.

questions.q: What is one advantage of living in the countryside?
opts: There is more space, fresh air and less noise
questions.fb: Espaço, ar puro e tranquilidade. Por outro lado, há menos serviços e lojas por perto.

questions.q: What is one disadvantage of living in a big city?
questions.fb: Trânsito, barulho e poluição são os problemas mais comuns das grandes cidades.

questions.q: What is the difference between a migrant and a refugee?
opts: A migrant chooses to move; a refugee is forced to leave
questions.fb: A diferença está na escolha: o migrante decide mudar; o refugiado foi obrigado a fugir.

questions.q: How can a community help refugees?
opts: By welcoming them, helping with language, school and housing
questions.fb: Acolher, ensinar a língua, garantir escola e moradia — é assim que uma comunidade recebe quem chega.

questions.q: What might a refugee family lose when they leave home?
opts: Their house, their school, their friends and sometimes their language
questions.fb: Perde-se muito mais do que a casa: escola, amigos, vizinhos e, às vezes, o convívio com a própria língua.
